newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power rises ahead of cooler weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power rises ahead of cooler weather.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. edged higher Tuesday on colder weather prospects later this week but was still at a discount to most other markets, industry sources said.

Firm, peak power in the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Wednesday delivery traded in the $22.00-23.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, as compared with Monday's $21.00-22.00 trading range.
"Prices are a bit higher today, but they still haven't recovered from last week. There are a lot of power marketers long," one market source said.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was notionally assessed around $15.00 in light trading, which is mostly unchanged.

At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Wednesday delivery were quoted in the $23.00-24.00 per MWh range, as compared with Monday's trading range around $22.00.
Firm, off-peak power for Wednesday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally assessed around $16.00-16.50.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to dip to about four to eight degrees Fahrenheit below-normal by Thursday.
Separately, the 900 megawatt (MW) Scherer 1 coal-fired unit in Georgia was shut Monday due to a boiler leak, Georgia Power, the operator said. The unit is expected to return to service Tuesday night.
